title: Across the stone valley · First look
focus: Longer words: Read a whole word before entering a longer letter sequence.

A clear signal and a careful look along the platform are more useful than a hurried departure that leaves someone uncertain about what to do. passage: A visitor can learn a great deal by watching what people check before they begin their work. "We've checked the visitor's note, but we haven't checked the team's copy," Mira said. "Don't change the original until both accounts agree." The reply was brief: "I'll compare them now." The harbor lies beyond the last row of houses. A path follows the water past wooden posts and low stone steps where the tide leaves little pools among the green weeds. A fishing boat rests beside the pier while its crew sorts a pile of rope. They lay the loops flat so that the line will run freely when the boat leaves the sheltered bay. The cafe near the bridge opens its blue door. Warm bread fills the air and a worker sets cups on the outside tables before the first walkers arrive from the hill above the town. A gull waits on the roof of the boat shed. It watches a basket move across the pier and calls once before turning toward the wide water where the morning light is growing brighter. The tide changes the shape of the shore each day. A dark stone that was hidden at breakfast can stand clear by noon while the narrow channels between the rocks grow deeper. A painter works on the rail beside the old ferry stop. The fresh coat will protect the wood from salt and rain while keeping the little landing easy to see from the water. The harbor office keeps a chart beneath a sheet of clear glass. Visitors can trace the route around the bay and find the safe crossing near the narrow mouth of the river.

title: The coastal garden · First look
focus: Colons and semicolons: Follow linked clauses with exact punctuation and spacing.
passage: A quiet visit leaves room to notice the details that a hurried journey might miss. The report separated 2 questions: what changed, and why? The first had a clear answer; the second needed another observation. "Record the uncertainty," Mira said. "A precise question is useful work." A path of flat stones leads past a bed of herbs. The leaves give off a fresh scent when a visitor brushes against them on the way toward the small gate at the far end. The gardeners choose plants that can live with dry summers. Thick leaves and deep roots help them use the little water that reaches the ground after a brief shower passes over the coast. A barrel under the shed roof catches rain for the young plants. The lid keeps leaves out while a mark on the side helps the team see how much water remains after each visit. Bees move between the yellow flowers beside the wall. The gardeners leave a quiet strip of long grass nearby so that small creatures have a place to rest when the beds are being tended. The compost heap warms slowly at the back of the garden. Dry leaves and kitchen scraps become dark soil that will feed a new bed after the rough pieces have had time to break down. A bench faces a gap in the wall where the sea comes into view. Walkers stop there to rest their bags and look at the pale line where the water seems to meet the distant sky. The team works from a simple sketch pinned inside the shed. Empty spaces on the plan leave room for new ideas without asking every plant to move whenever someone brings a fresh seed.
